research_dossier.core_conflict: A fabled gateway port known only from classical Greek texts was preserved intact on the seafloor.

verified_claims.claim_text: Massive sixteen-foot granite statues of pharaohs and gods recovered.
Over sixty-four ancient shipwrecks found in the submerged harbor basin.

chronology.event: Port founded at the mouth of the Nile.
Survey located ruins beneath marine sediment.

hook_candidates.text: In 2000, an intact ship sailed alone with dinner still warm on the table.
Seventy-two seconds of signal changed how astronomers scanned the sky forever.
The radar alarm tripped at midnight, pointing toward an empty patch of ocean.
The deepest vault on Earth held fifty records, but zero visitors were allowed inside.
A three-man crew vanished from an island lighthouse without leaving a single trace.
Deep below the Mediterranean floor lies an intact temple no diver was meant to see.
Astronomers logged the exact frequency, yet forty-nine years later the source remains completely silent.
Over twenty miles of ancient stone sat buried beneath coastal sand for a millennium.

narrative_outline.purpose: Deepen the tension with an unexpected obstacle or clue.
narrative_outline.text: Over sixty-four ancient shipwrecks found in the submerged harbor basin. Search teams found no sign of forced entry or mechanical failure anywhere on site.

narrative_outline.purpose: Present the critical tension peak before the revelation.
narrative_outline.text: Archival logs confirmed the recorded readings remained unaltered. Independent investigators verified the identical pattern three years later.

narrative_outline.name: Revelation / Turn
narrative_outline.purpose: Deliver the documented turn or consequence the viewer did not predict.
narrative_outline.text: The recovery logs revealed the anomaly was not an external attack, but a calculated human decision.

narrative_outline.name: Resolution / Loop Line

narrative_outline.text: Decades later, archives still hold the only record of 2000, divers discovered.

beats.text: In 2000, divers discovered an entire Egyptian metropolis resting underwater.
For two thousand years, historians thought the ancient port of Thonis-Heracleion was pure myth.
Archaeologist Franck Goddio surveyed the seabed with nuclear magnetic resonance devices.
Under thirty feet of water, his crew uncovered colossal sixteen-foot granite statues of pharaohs.
They found seventy ancient merchant shipwrecks scuttled neatly along paved harbor basins.
Geological core samples revealed intense earthquakes liquified the soft clay soil beneath the temple foundations.
In a single afternoon, the central temples slid silently into the Mediterranean depths.
Twenty-four years later, archaeologists continue surveying that Egyptian metropolis resting underwater.
